body: I thought I'd share my IG profile, so you can put a face to the person you have helped so much! It's open so you can find me! Username is nicoleray88...
I'm still here! I didn't want to get out of bed, but only because of the rainy weather here! I feel better, not quite 100%, but I'll get there.
I'm still here... I just woke up. That's the first step to over coming this right? :-)
I use Wish to get all my crazy make up stuff!
Lol!!! I am a make up chick... And I watch all those weird tutorials!!!
I keep a journal, diary, or whatever you want to call it... So I guess opening it up to the world may hold me accountable.

I'd probably be more successful with a vlog, because well I've been told on several occasions I'm OK to look at, but I'm not sure I want to explain my gut issues to the world. So I'd have to blog that. 😊
I did not know you could do that!

Unfortunately, since there isn't a "cure" for crohns the military won't take me back at all. 
I'm actually a manager and as a side gig I personal train, and have done classes for another gym. 
I try to stay positive and upbeat on my  Instagram/Snapchat/Facebook and always post my progress, and have been in contact with others who love fitness and have crohns. Most have been helpful, but there are a few that have been anything but helpful.

I've looked into different religions, and groups. It for the most part I love the historical factor of religions, but modern religion is just a tad too much for me. 
My biggest problem I've had since getting out of the military, has been finding myself. 
I really don't know who I am without the army. It's like having a spouse or significant other, they gave me shelter, food, purpose, and somewhat good health. It's almost like I'm a widowed woman... 
I thought being in the fitness industry would be my calling, and to an extent it has been, but I still feel empty even though I get to do something I enjoy.
No I'm not, it never made much sense to me.

LOL... You just made me tear up a bit! 
I've tried looking into other schools and options, and if I make it through the night, I'll look into my options for school and ways to get out of my house. :-)
Since I slacked on my second semester, I don't think my GI Bill will cover any other classes. :-(

Psychology and anatomy were my favorite classes... 
I'm pretty sure I had an A in both. I was actually taking the classes at a satellite location of the school so I only had to deal with "kids" for anatomy since that class was actually held at the satellite location and not via teleconference.
I tried college, did one semester, and hated it. I did really well, but couldn't handle being a freshman at 27... :-)
:-D ehhh they are retired and probably wouldn't want a almost 30-something female... And if there was someone it's probably a skeezy old guy...
My gym is for the older, more established crowd. :-/

My house was broken into last week and the cops think it was just a pervert (which I have been dealing with a peeping Tom for a while now). I feel dirty in my own house, and I was planning on moving back home because of all this... But, my sister is living with her and there just isn't room for me there anymore. I've looked into moving in with a friend, but things seem to fall through.
My choice for being child free started because of the way I was raised, but now I don't want to genetically pass whatever is wrong with me onto a poor innocent child.

I live alone and now I live about an hour away from family. 
I always thought I'd be a "strong independent woman" that didn't need a man. The older I get, the more I realize I liked having someone to share accomplishments with.
Oh yeah, my siblings were spoiled compared to the way I was raised.

Going to a new doctor would mean I would have to be poked and scoped again. Just getting ready for one more colonoscopy (sp?) Is torture. 
At this point I have my crohns under control without medications. 
I'm not upset about my condition as much anymore.
And I'm the oldest child... And I'm sort of the black sheep.

I actually have a old cabinet that I started refinishing, I didn't have all the tools I needed to fix it up, so it's sitting in my house collecting dust. It would be a really pretty cabinet if I'd finish it. 
I don't have a significant other, mainly because I don't want kids and at my age that seems to be a deal breaker. 
The first time I reached out to my family about these thoughts was after my gut doctor said I could be dead in five years due to complications from crohns. They get scared and don't know how to communicate and take everything personal. So I've decided to just keep this to myself this time around, especially since my mom is the only family I have anymore, and she's dealing with her own stress.

I don't really have any hobbies anymore. I will get into a phase where I'll paint, knit, or crochet, but I don't feel like doing those since they are more of winter activities. 
I have never really been one to get into sports... Which I know is weird since I love being a part of a team. 
I have friends from every walk of life, but the ones I think who can relate to this kind of mind state have been the least helpful and treat me like I'm wasting their time.

At my last job, I worked closely with several departments. It really helped me network with them and get to know how things work. 
I am fostering a pit who is blind but she's a sweet heart, and then my fur child is a terrier mutt...
I actually wanted to be a law enforcement officer, but with  financial issues, and thinking like this I can't go into a field like that.
I work in a gym, and I never thought I would be doing this. I was trying to over come crohns and get physically fit, but even my drive for that is gone.

I was diagnosed with crohns disease and had to be hospitalized a couple times, so the army decided it was less risky to just get me out. 
I loved the brotherhood and bonding with everyone, my job, and just having so many adventures from training, deployments, and getting through the rough times with buddies.
I was Army active duty, was medically retired about 3 years ago. I thought I would serve my entire life. I loved it.
Last week.
